AMGN.rationale: AMGN presents a moderately attractive setup anchored by a rare valuation dislocation: PE of 23.4× sits at the floor of its 365-day range (22.6–49.7×), with earnings yield of 4.3% essentially at parity with the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.47% — a condition unseen for this franchise in the lookback period. The fundamental basis for the de-rating is partly real (Prolia -33.85% patent cliff, Tavneos FDA withdrawal risk, IRS tax dispute) and partly mechanical (Q1 2026 EPS reset the trailing denominator). However, the underlying business trajectory is healthier than the price action suggests: Q1 2026 revenue beat consensus by 1.4%, adjusted EPS beat by 8%, gross profit grew +13.4% YoY on only +5.8% revenue growth (operating leverage), OCF grew +57.4% YoY, and six growth drivers collectively grew 24% YoY with 17 products at $1B+ run rate. Management raised full-year guidance to $37.1B–$38.5B revenue and $21.70–$23.10 non-GAAP EPS. The primary offset is balance-sheet leverage at 6.2× debt/equity ($57.32B debt vs $9.19B equity), which is elevated and deteriorating, and the patent cliff is a confirmed multi-billion-dollar headwind. The Tavneos overhang and IRS dispute add idiosyncratic risk. On balance, the valuation discount appears to overstate the fundamental deterioration — the growth engine is demonstrably working and margins are expanding — but the leverage and near-term headwinds prevent a higher conviction score. The Q1 earnings beat and guidance raise serve as a modest near-term catalyst, though the stock declined post-earnings due to Tavneos/IRS noise, leaving the re-rating incomplete.
